Hi Anna —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top, details below:

- EU default placement: yes — for your org we can pin inference to EU-only capacity (our EU region footprint) by contract and provisioning. That means customer traffic is routed to EU-only runtime variants unless you elect an explicit failover.
- Transient cross-hop: triggers are limited to three scenarios: 1) cache pre-warming for hot keys when EU pool capacity is saturated and a configured burst window is active; 2) telemetry/analytics aggregation for metrics pipelines that customers opt into; 3) incident-driven inspection (only with customer approval or as required by law). Hi Anna — looping in for the technical detail. See answers inline and attached architecture snippet (arch-diagram-egress.svg).

On Tue, Apr 27, 2027 at 11:22 AM Anna Greer <anna.greer@sablehealth.com> wrote:
> - "Burst window" semantics: can you define the capacity threshold and the max number of minutes per calendar day that pre-warming can occur? Our policy requires an option to cap or opt-out.

We expose two knobs you can set in the org config:
- Burst threshold: a percent of allocated GPU pool utilization (default 85%). If the pool utilization for a 60s sliding window exceeds that threshold, prefix-level pre-warming may be scheduled to reduce tail latency.
- Burst window cap: configurable in minutes/day (default 30m/day). We can set to 0 to opt out of any cross-region pre-warm behavior.

> - For telemetry that leaves the EU for metrics processing: will you pseudonymize before egress? Which fields are guaranteed removed or hashed?

Yes — for the metrics pipeline we pseudonymize identifiers prior to any egress. PII fields are excluded entirely. The stream includes: event_type, timestamp, pseudonymized_client_id, model_id, latency_ms, error_code. No raw request text or embeddings are included in that stream unless you explicitly enable embedding-level analytics (which is off by default).

> - Auditability: we need IDed audit log samples showing a transient-hop event with timestamps and the triggering reason.

Attached to this thread are redacted audit samples and the arch-diagram showing the routing decision logic. We can provide a structured CSV with the same fields for your auditors under an NDA.

> KMS: do you support customer-managed keys for EU-only instances?

Short answer: yes. We support KMS integrations for Dedicated/Private deployments and offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) option for Hosted customers via a Cloud HSM-backed key escrow for EU instances. Keys can be region-bound per the addendum.

Next steps: I’ll update the DPA addendum language with the knobs described above and hand to Legal.
